passages.original: — Nam primum ea, quae (i) Nicaeae Thraciae omnium impie- tas resolvisset, sancta 598 esse testator : vim scili- cet illatam episcopis, fidem esse verae confessionis affirmans. Negat quoque se scire Arium : cum in Alexandria in (j) Ariana ecclesia, cui Gregorius praeerat, presbyter esse coepisset. Sed de Ariminen- si synodo, quae ab omnibus est religiose dissoluta, nihil dicamus : tantum diaboli commenta pandenda sunt.
passages.english: For first he testifies that those things which the impiety of all had undone at Nicaea in Thrace are holy, asserting, that is, that the force brought to bear on the bishops is the faith of true confession. He also denies that he knows Arius, although he had begun to be a presbyter at Alexandria in the Arian church over which Gregory presided. But let us say nothing about the synod of Ariminum, which has been dissolved by all in a religious spirit; only the devil's inventions must be laid open.
passages.notes: The text reads 'quae ... omnium impietas resolvisset'; the sense of 'resolvisset' (here 'undone') is uncertain, and the phrase may refer to what the general impiety 'settled' or 'released' at Nicaea in Thrace (the council of Nike, 359). The letters (i), (j) and the number 598 are editorial footnote or page marks and have been omitted. 'Testator' is taken as 'testatur'.
